﻿
This guide presents a comprehensive outline for a tax diligence memorandum focused on S-election risks and exposure. This structure is designed to guide a detailed analysis, ensuring all critical aspects of S-corporation status, qualification, and potential pitfalls are addressed.

Tax Diligence Memorandum Outline: S-Election Risks and Exposure
I. Introduction
    • Purpose of Memorandum 
        ◦ Scope of review (e.g., acquisition, investment, internal compliance)
        ◦ Summary of target entity and transaction context
    • Executive Summary 
        ◦ Key findings and recommendations
II. Overview of S-Corporation Status
    • Definition and Benefits of S-Corporation Election
    • Summary of S-Election Requirements (IRC §1361, §1362) 
        ◦ Eligible entities
        ◦ Shareholder requirements
        ◦ Stock requirements
        ◦ Election process and timing
III. S-Election Qualification Review
    • Entity Eligibility 
        ◦ Domestic corporation status
        ◦ Ineligible entity types (e.g., certain financial institutions, insurance companies)
    • Shareholder Eligibility 
        ◦ Permitted shareholders (individuals, certain trusts, estates)
        ◦ Prohibited shareholders (nonresident aliens, partnerships, corporations)
        ◦ Number of shareholders (100-shareholder limit)
    • Stock Structure 
        ◦ Single class of stock requirement
        ◦ Review of equity instruments (convertibles, options, warrants, debt instruments)
    • Election Process 
        ◦ Timeliness and validity of Form 2553 filing
        ◦ Unanimous shareholder consent
IV. Historical Compliance and Maintenance of S-Status
    • Review of Corporate Records 
        ◦ Articles of incorporation, bylaws, shareholder agreements
        ◦ Stock ledgers and transfer records
    • Prior and Ongoing Compliance 
        ◦ Changes in ownership or structure
        ◦ Issuance of new equity or debt
        ◦ Distributions and redemptions
    • Potential Inadvertent Terminations 
        ◦ Violations of eligibility requirements
        ◦ Issuance of a second class of stock
        ◦ Nonresident alien shareholders
        ◦ Late or defective elections
V. Tax Exposure and Risk Assessment
    • Consequences of S-Status Termination 
        ◦ Reversion to C-corporation status
        ◦ Built-in gains tax exposure
        ◦ Loss of pass-through treatment
    • Potential IRS Challenges 
        ◦ Audit risk factors
        ◦ Prior IRS correspondence or examinations
    • State and Local Tax Considerations 
        ◦ Conformity with federal S-election
        ◦ Separate state-level S-election requirements
VI. Remediation and Corrective Actions
    • IRS Relief for Inadvertent Terminations (IRC §1362(f)) 
        ◦ Eligibility for relief
        ◦ Required corrective actions and filings
    • Prospective Risk Mitigation 
        ◦ Recommendations for ongoing compliance
        ◦ Shareholder and entity agreement amendments
VII. Transaction-Specific Considerations
    • Impact on Proposed Transaction 
        ◦ Change of control implications
        ◦ Section 338(h)(10) or Section 336(e) elections
        ◦ Buyer and seller indemnities
    • Representations and Warranties 
        ◦ Drafting considerations for purchase agreements
VIII. Conclusion and Recommendations
    • Summary of Key Risks
    • Recommended Next Steps
    • Open Issues for Further Diligence
IX. Exhibits and Supporting Documentation
    • Checklist of S-Election Requirements
    • Sample Forms and Filings
    • Summary Table of Identified Risks
